unit.unitTitle: Hello — Listening and Saying Your Name

cefr.bandName: Pre-A1, from no English at all

unit.unitOverview:
Say hello and goodbye. Say your name. Say yes and no.
You do not have to read yet. Listen first. Letters come in Unit 2.
unit.learningPath:
Listen to the lesson. Do not read.
Words: listen, then say each one.
Patterns: I am, your name, yes and no.
Listen to three short talks.
Speak. Record. Listen back.
Copy your name.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
functions: Say hello and goodbye at the right moment
Ask another person for their name
Say please, thank you and sorry
Answer a question with yes or no
Do what the teacher says: listen, look, say, stop
unit.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

visual.lectureScript:
Hello. This is Unit 1.
You do not have to read today. Just listen.
First word: hello. Listen. Hello.
Say it with me. Hello.
When you go away, you say goodbye. Goodbye.
Say it with me. Goodbye.
Now your name. I am Sara. My name is Sara.
Your turn. Say: I am, and then your name.
Say it now.
Good. Now we ask. What is your name?
Say it with me. What is your name?
There are two small answers in English. Yes and no.
Are you Ben? No. I am Sara.
Are you here? Yes. I am here.
Three more words. Please. Thank you. Sorry.
You want a pen. You say: a pen, please.
I give you the pen. You say: thank you.
You do not hear me. You say: sorry?
Last, four words from your teacher.
Listen. Look. Say. Stop.
Listen means use your ears.
Look means use your eyes.
Say means make a word with your mouth.
Stop means do not go on.
That is Unit 1. Now go to the words and listen again.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: I am, and my name is
grammar.explanation:
Say who you are in two ways.
Both are right.
Use am only after I.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I am Sara.
My name is Sara.

I am Ben.
My name is Ben.

I → am
my name → is
grammar.workedExample:
Your name is Ana.
1. Start with I.
2. After I, use am.
3. Then your name.
4. Say: I am Ana.
5. The other way: My name is Ana.
grammar.commonMistake:
Many languages have no word here.
English needs am or is.
No: I Ana.
Yes: I am Ana.
No: My name Ana.
Yes: My name is Ana.
grammar.memoryTip: Am goes with I. Only with I.
grammar.practice:
Say each one with your own name.
1. I ___ …
2. My name ___ …
3. ___ am …
4. My ___ is …
grammar.answerKey:
1. am
2. is
3. I
4. name
All four right? Go on.
Wrong on 1 or 3? Am always goes with I.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: What is your name?
grammar.explanation:
Ask a person for their name.
The question has four words.
Your voice goes down at the end.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
What is your name?

A: What is your name?
B: My name is Ana.

A: What is your name?
B: I am Ben.
grammar.workedExample:
You meet a new person.
1. Say hello.
2. Say your own name first.
3. Then ask: What is your name?
4. Listen. Say their name back.
5. Say: Nice to meet you.
grammar.commonMistake:
Do not say: What your name?
English needs is.
Yes: What is your name?
grammar.memoryTip: Say your own name first. Then ask.
grammar.practice:
Put the words in order.
1. name / your / what / is
2. is / Ana / my / name
3. Ben / am / I
grammar.answerKey:
1. What is your name?
2. My name is Ana.
3. I am Ben.
Wrong on 1? The question word what comes first.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Yes and no
grammar.explanation:
Yes and no are whole answers.
You can say more after them.
Not is the word that makes it no.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Are you Ana?
Yes. / Yes, I am.
No. / No, I am not.

Are you here?
Yes, I am here.
No, I am not here.
grammar.workedExample:
Someone asks: Are you Ben?
1. Is it true? No.
2. Say no.
3. Then say who you are.
4. Say: No, I am Sara.
grammar.commonMistake:
No: I am no Ben.
Yes: I am not Ben.
No is the answer. Not goes in the sentence.
grammar.memoryTip: After no, say who you really are.
grammar.practice:
Answer about yourself.
1. Are you a teacher?
2. Are you here?
3. Are you late?
4. Is your name Omar?
grammar.answerKey:
Any true answer is right.
Check: did you start with yes or no?
Did you use am or am not after it?

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Please, thank you and sorry
grammar.explanation:
Three words that open doors.
Please when you ask.
Thank you when you get.
Sorry for a mistake.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Ask → please
A pen, please.

Get → thank you
Thank you!

Mistake → sorry
Sorry, I am late.

Not hear → Sorry?
grammar.workedExample:
You want water.
1. Ask: Water, please.
2. You get it.
3. Say: Thank you.
4. You did not hear the answer.
5. Say: Sorry?
grammar.commonMistake:
Please can go at the end of an ask.
Best: Water, please.
Also right: Please give me water.
grammar.memoryTip: Please and thank you are never wrong.
grammar.practice:
Which word?
1. You want a book. ___
2. You get the book. ___
3. You are late. ___
4. You did not hear. ___
grammar.answerKey:
1. please
2. thank you
3. sorry
4. sorry
Wrong on 4? Sorry has two uses: a mistake, and not hearing.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Listen first. Do not read.
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Tap Listen. Do not look at the words.
You will hear five things.
1. hello
2. goodbye
3. please
4. thank you
5. sorry
Listen two times.
Now tap the mic. Say all five back.
Tap again. Listen to yourself.
Check: five words? In the same order?
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Ask the tutor to say the five words in a new order. Say each one back.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 2 — Say your own name
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Say three lines about yourself.
1. Hello.
2. I am (your name).
3. My name is (your name).
Tap the mic. Say the three lines.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: did you say am after I?
Is your name clear and not fast?
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Say your name to the tutor. Ask it to say your name back to you.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Ask for a name
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Hello! B: Hello!
2. A: I am Ana. B: What is your name?
3. A: My name is Ben. B: Nice to meet you.
4. A: Goodbye! B: Goodbye!
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Tap again. Listen.
Check: is there is in your question?
A friend can say A. No one with you? Say A and B.
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Ask the tutor for its name. Listen. Then say its name back to check it.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Yes or no about you
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Listen to five questions. Answer about yourself.
1. Are you here?
2. Are you a teacher?
3. Is your name Omar?
4. Are you late?
5. Are you happy?
Tap the mic. Say five answers.
Start each one with yes or no.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: five answers? Yes or no first in each one?
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Ask the tutor to ask you four questions about yourself. Answer yes or no to each.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Listen, look, say, stop
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Tap Listen. Do what you hear.
Listen.
Look at the door.
Say your name.
Stop.
Do it two times.
Now tap the mic. Say the four words yourself.
Check: did you do each one, not just say it?
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Ask the tutor to give you four instructions. Do each one. Then give it four.

speaking.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Hello and goodbye, all together
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
Listen and repeat.
he-LLO. Hello.
good-BYE. Goodbye.
The second part is strong in both.
Not HE-llo. he-LLO.
Now say them in a line.
Hello. My name is (your name). Goodbye.
Tap the mic. Say the line. Tap again. Listen.
Check: is the second part strong in hello and goodbye?
speaking.aiTutorPrompt: Say hello to the tutor. Ask it which part of the word was strong.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Copy your name
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Copy your own name.
Write it three times.
Write on the line, left to right.
writing.successCriteria:
Three times.
The same letters each time.
The first letter is a capital.
Every letter sits on the line.
writing.support:
Copy it one letter at a time.
Look at the model after every letter.
writing.extension: Now write it once without looking. Then check.

writing.promptAndInstructions:
Copy the two words.
Write each one two times.
writing.successCriteria:
Four words on the page.
The letters are in the right order.
There is a space between the words.
writing.support: Copy hello only. Do goodbye tomorrow.
writing.extension: Add please and thank you, copied from the word list.

activities.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
activities.title: Practice 1 — Which word do you hear?
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Tap Listen. You will hear one word each time.
Choose the word you hear.
1. hello / goodbye
2. please / sorry
3. yes / no
4. name / same
5. listen / look
6. stop / say
7. thank you / hello
8. I / my
activities.answerSummary:
1. hello
2. please
3. yes
4. name
5. listen
6. stop
7. thank you
8. I
Six or more right: good.
Below six: listen to the lesson again.
activities.soloPath: Answer out loud, then open Check yourself.

activities.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
activities.title: Practice 2 — Say it back
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Tap Listen. Say each line back.
1. Hello.
2. My name is Ana.
3. What is your name?
4. Yes, I am.
5. No, I am not.
6. Thank you.
activities.answerSummary:
There is no wrong answer here.
Check: did you say all six?
Did you wait for the line to finish first?
activities.soloPath: Record all six, then listen back once.

activities.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
activities.title: Practice 3 — Yes or no
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Answer about yourself. Say yes or no.
1. Are you here?
2. Is your name Ben?
3. Are you a student?
4. Are you a teacher?
5. Are you happy?
6. Are you late?
activities.answerSummary:

Check: did you start each one with yes or no?
Five or six answered: good.
activities.soloPath: Say your six answers out loud before you look.

activities.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
activities.title: Practice 4 — Do what you hear
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Tap Listen. Do the thing.
1. Listen.
2. Look at the door.
3. Say your name.
4. Stop.
Do it two times.
activities.answerSummary:
1. You were quiet and still.
2. You turned to the door.
3. You said your name.
4. You stopped.
All four: good. You can follow your teacher.
activities.soloPath: Do it alone. Then do it again and check yourself.

activities.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
activities.title: Practice 5 — Hello or goodbye?
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Say hello or goodbye.
1. You come in the door. ___
2. You go out the door. ___
3. You meet a new person. ___
4. The class is finished. ___
5. Your friend comes to you. ___
6. Your friend goes away. ___
activities.answerSummary:
1. hello
2. goodbye
3. hello
4. goodbye
5. hello
6. goodbye
All six right? You know the two words.
activities.soloPath: Say your answers out loud first.

activities.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
activities.title: Practice 6 — Find the name
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Look at the list. Do not read every letter. Look at the shape.
Ana   Ben   Omar   Sara   Lee
1. Which name is the shortest?
2. Which name is the longest?
3. Which two names start with the same letter?
4. Is your own name in the list?
5. How many names are there?
activities.answerSummary:
1. Lee (or Ana — both are three letters; Lee and Ana are the shortest)
2. Omar or Sara (four letters)
3. None of them start with the same letter
4. Any true answer
5. Five
Four or five right: you can find a word by its shape. That is reading beginning.
activities.soloPath: Look, then answer. Do not sound the letters out yet.

teacherNotes.note: The unit is built for a learner alone. Every pattern card has a worked example before its practice, every practice has an answer key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check. If you are helping, sit beside rather than lead.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.note: This is the first unit of a level for adults who may not read the Latin script at all. Every reading text is one the learner has already met by ear, and every comprehension question can be answered from the recording alone. Do not ask a learner to read aloud in this unit. Letters arrive as shapes in Unit 2 and as names in Unit 3.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.note: An adult beginner needs longer to answer than feels comfortable. Count to five in your head before you help. Most learners get there on four.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
teacherNotes.noteType: The learner's own name is the first text
teacherNotes.note: Writing 1 asks the learner to copy their own name. That is the single most motivating thing on the page and often the first English a learner ever writes. Give it real time, and keep the model in front of them.

teacherNotes.note: Unit 2 teaches the 26 letters as shapes and Unit 3 as names. Level 1 Unit 0 then teaches the same letters and blending again. That repeat is deliberate: a learner who starts at Level 1 still meets the alphabet, and a learner who comes through Intro meets it as revision.

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Hello — Hello is for meeting. Goodbye is for going away.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Goodbye — Goodbye is the word for going away.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Thank you — Thank you is for when you get a thing. Please is for when you ask.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: am — Am always goes with I. Is goes with he, she or a name.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: is — My name is one thing, so it takes is. Am only goes with I.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: What is your name? — It starts with what and ends with a question mark.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: No, I am Sara. — The answer is no. Then you say who you are.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Use your ears — Listen means use your ears. Look means use your eyes.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Use your eyes — Look means use your eyes.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Sorry? — Sorry has two uses. One is for a mistake. One is when you do not hear.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Omar — A name starts with a capital letter. The others are not names.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: A pen, please. — Please makes an ask polite. Without it the ask sounds like an order.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
